## Problem

Hook liveness asks "is any process with `claude` in its command line running anywhere on this machine?": `(*claude.Detector).IsRunning()` runs `pgrep -f claude` (`internal/agent/claude/process.go:12`). When a session has ended and the user makes a manual commit while any other Claude process runs, pre-commit treats the session as live, and the manual commit gets agent attribution.

The recorded `agent_pid` does not fix this: `AgentPID()` returns `PgrepFirst("claude")` (`internal/agent/claude/process.go:25-26`), the first process whose command line contains "claude". Checked 2026-10-10 (argos review): each Claude Code tool shell matches too, because its command line holds `~/.claude/shell-snapshots/…`. So a liveness check of the recorded PID tests an arbitrary Claude process, not the owner of the session.

## Proposed feature

1. In pre-commit, walk the parent chain of the hook process (Linux: field 4 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`; macOS: `ps -o ppid= -p <pid>`) and match the executable name (`/proc/<pid>/comm`, or the base name of argv[0]) against the agent names (`claude`, `codex`), not a substring of the command line. An agent ancestor means that this commit runs inside that agent session; store its PID as `agent_pid`. Checked on Linux: a Claude Code tool shell has the `claude` process as its second parent.
2. Use the liveness of that PID (`isProcessAlive`, already in `internal/session/cleanup.go`) for the session-end and condensed-session skip decisions.
3. When no agent is an ancestor (a commit from a normal terminal), keep today's global detection as the fallback, so capture does not regress for users who commit agent work by hand. Log at debug level which path decided.

Related: the attribution design call (#342, #372, #396, #755, #457, #564).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A commit run from an agent tool shell finds the agent PID through the parent chain and stores it as `agent_pid`
- [ ] The match uses the executable name, so a shell whose command line contains `.claude` is not an agent
- [ ] A commit from a terminal with no agent ancestor uses the fallback, and the debug log says so
- [ ] Session-end and condensed-session decisions use the liveness of the stored PID when it exists
- [ ] Unit tests cover a live PID, a dead PID, an absent PID, and a parent chain with and without an agent
- [ ] A second commit during a live session still gets its `Partio-Checkpoint` trailer
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass

Proposal id: session-pid-liveness
